definition.label: Keep a pet
definition.intro: Tell the committee about the animal you want to keep.

fields.label: It is registered with the council (dogs/cats)

deadline.banner: If the committee hasn't decided by the end of {date}, this pet request is treated as APPROVED.
deadline.citation: SM s 58A(2), s 69(1)(b)(ii), s 69(3)(b); law file §5-6 — DRAFT
deadline.if_missed: Treated as approved if not decided within 21 days of the request (SM s 58A, s 69(3)(b)) — DRAFT, to be checked against Altai's by-laws

steps.title: Check the request against the animals by-law
Ask for anything missing (registration, photos)
Decide, with reasons if refused, before the deadline
Tell the resident and record any conditions

stages.label: New
stages.rule: Given to the secretary (chair if the secretary is absent): SM s 58A(2) — DRAFT
stages.instructions: Check the form is complete, then acknowledge it so the resident knows it's in hand. The clock started when it was lodged, not when it was opened.

email.subject: {ref}: we have your request
{ref}: we need a bit more from you

stages.label: Checking
stages.rule: Act s 169B(6); BCCM Office 'Animal by-laws' — DRAFT
stages.instructions: Check it against the animals by-law. It may be refused only for: an unacceptable health or safety risk conditions can't manage; it breaks a law; a regulated dog; unreasonable interference conditions can't manage; or the owner refuses reasonable conditions. 'No pets' is never a reason. Then put it to the committee.

buttons.label: Put it to a committee vote

email.subject: {ref}: we need a bit more from you

stages.label: Committee deciding
stages.instructions: Each voting member votes in the portal. A motion outside a meeting passes when a majority of ALL members entitled to vote say yes; it fails when half or more say no.

email.subject: {ref}: your vote is needed

stages.label: Decided
stages.rule: SM s 69(4); SM s 73(1)(e): an animal approval can be acted on at once — DRAFT
stages.instructions: The resident was emailed the decision when it was recorded. Note any conditions on the record, then close it.
